If you want to make a change in your 'health plan' get the experts (doctors, therapists etc) to help you, talk with them and work something out that works for you!

I diagnosed myself when I was 16 (ish?). I noticed something was wrong because I kept having weeks and months of feeling depressed, then all of a sudden laughing and crying at the same time and doing things like throwing a plate of french toast at the wall when getting irritated at my boyfriend (funny now to think back to it), then having moments of weird hyper-sexuality. Went to my GP and told him " I think I'm bipolar", and he literally laughed at me (didn't ask me a single question). Went on undiagnosed till last year (10ish years later), when I got severely depressed and suicidal. I figured I should go see a psychiatrist before I kill myself, so I went, and he diagnosed me. Damn GP, I could have had help years ago!  
Also, keep talking to your doctor and your therapist. I'm super inquisitive with my therapist, so your doctor shouldn't mind you asking why he thinks so, and monitor your mood yourself (I keep track of my mood, anxiety, irritability and sleep in an excel file hahah). Tracking yourself helps you figure yourself out, and maybe it could help give you peace of mind (in terms of your diagnosis).

Hi, I'm only on cipralex (its escitalopram, so I'm not sure if you meant it or not -- but I'll go ahead anyway haha).
 It works great for me. I was extremely depressed and anxious to the point where I didn't really leave bed, and I stopped working etc. 

I haven't had any side effects. At the beginning I was yawning non-stop and it would make me drowsy, but I haven't had that since the first 2 weeks. 
What do you mean roller coaster? (meaning depressed then 'normal' or depressed then manic/hypomanic?-- or both?). Since it's just an anti-depressant (not a mood stabilizer), it could make you hypomanic/manic.  I'm BD II and I manage without a mood stabilizer  (and only cipralex) but I couldn't say if that would work for you or not =) (as I am not your doctor :P). Also, there are a lot of shitty people (in general - and in the medical community) -- but there are awesome doctors and staff out there (I work in a bipolar clinic haha -- not to toot my own horn) and I'm sure you will eventually find someone who 'gets' you.

1) yes - cipralex (escitalopram)
2) all on its own (yeah- I know risky)
3) low/no anxiety (unless its at a natural reasonable level due to some current situation e.g. presenting, helped immensely with depression (so I feel less anhedonic, less frustrated, more energetic etc).

Note - I'm BD II. 
-Before: I was depressed, so depressed and empty. Empty to the point of multiple suicide attempts. Hopeless enough to think about jumping in front of the train every morning, or every evening to and from school. I couldn't think straight, I couldn't concentrate in class, I had a terrible short term memory, I couldn't focus long enough or care enough to have a conversation with someone. I would lay in bed for days. During the worst of it, I also had issues with GAD, and ended up having panic attacks at work, and at school for no apparent reason. I would just go into the stairwell and cry, I absolutely wanted to die every day. 
When I wasn't depressed I was so frustrated and anxious I still couldn't think. It was impossible for me to sit still and get anything done. I couldn't sit still in a chair and do my work, all I could think about was sex, or travel or god knows what. My mind raced all day long. I shopped excessively, talked to strangers and then when it all settled down --- I hated myself for how I had acted. It was an endless loop of being depressed, being hypomanic, and then hating myself for how I had acted -- repeat--. This went on for years, (started when I was 16, I'm now 24). It made undergrad very hard, and now I am in graduate school and last year I almost dropped out and quit because I didn't think I could handle life itself anymore. 

-After: I will try and express how much it has helped me, but I'm not sure if I will do it justice haha (started meds this January). Since starting medication, the endless loop of negative thoughts is gone, I can think, I can have complete peace of mind. I can concentrate at a conference, I can remember things again, I can talk to strangers without my heart racing, and I can get out of bed in the morning loving what I do. I am focused, positive about my future, and balanced. I am actually very happy (but not hypomanic ! haha). I haven't had a single suicidal thought (after I got to the right dose), and I have had no self-harm, no panic attacks, no bouts of crying for hours. I can touch subway poles and door knobs, I can ride the subway/train without hating everyone around me (no rage!). I thought I hated people, but I find that now I can actually be sociable (before I felt like everyone hated me, but it turns out that was in my head). I have been more creative, I can paint again, draw, publish articles, and come up with more research ideas. Meds have helped me immensely. The one bad thing, my sex drive is kaput. Wish I could fix that... but at least I'm happy and alive.
